title: Durable vision/charter and resumable progress artifacts
description:
Gives jit-project-lead a durable vision/charter document — the project vision plus a first-class decision log of chosen and rejected options with reasons — and a resumable project-level progress file, both of which survive across sessions.

## Background

The vision/charter must outlive any single work item's completion, so it lands under a `permanent_paths` location (never auto-archived) read from the project's documentation config (`permanent_paths = ["docs/"]` in this repo's `.jit/config.toml`). The progress file is operational state meaningful only while the top-level strategic container is active, so it lives under `dev/active/<strategic-container-short-id>-progress.json`, a one-tier-up analogue of the per-epic progress file `jit-execution-lead` already produces, with per-sub-strategic-container rows instead of per-issue rows.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A vision/charter document exists at a location read from the project's documentation config, containing the vision and a decision log entry for every consequential decision recording what was chosen, what was rejected, and why.
- [hard] REQ-02: A project-level progress file exists at `dev/active/<strategic-container-short-id>-progress.json`, tracking per-sub-strategic-container status analogous to the per-issue rows in `jit-execution-lead`'s progress file.
- [hard] REQ-03: Both artifacts are linked to the strategic container via `jit doc`.
- [hard] REQ-04: Re-invoking jit-project-lead on the same strategic container reads back both the vision/charter and the progress state and resumes without losing prior decisions or progress.

## Notes

Vision/charter placement in `docs/` (not `dev/active`) is deliberate: a milestone-level vision has no natural end-of-life, so it must not be subject to archival on container completion. The progress file, by contrast, is fine to archive when the container completes — its `dev/active` location is intentional, not an oversight.
